skills: Lesson m15l03: Writing the change request: problem, impact, proposal, alternatives, risk, verification

title: Negotiation, version control and closure with post-change data

goals.text: Write and defend an ECN/DCR request against typical design objections.
Build an evidence pack that quantifies the process impact of the current design.

blocks.alt: A negotiation exchange between process and design, a version-controlled drawing revision block, and a post-change capability chart
blocks.caption: Negotiation, version control and closure with post-change data

theory.h: Frame the ECN or DCR as a controlled problem statement
p: An ECN or DCR starts with a measurable problem, not a preference.

State the affected assembly, part numbers, revision, production quantity and the process step where the defect appears, plus the current controlled documents: drawing revision, land pattern per IPC-7351, stencil thickness, paste type, feeder map, AOI program and reflow profile per IPC-7530.

If the change is only a temporary containment, label it as one, so nobody files it as a design improvement. Use IPC-7711/7721 for rework and repair limits only when discussing repairability, not as a substitute for design change data.
Use at least 30 consecutive production days or 1000 boards, whichever gives a stable sample, and check the sample size against your MES capability.
Report boards started, boards passed, rework events, scrap, test escapes, cycle time and downtime. Separate common-cause variation from special-cause events.
For defect classification, use the acceptability class the contract requires under IPC-A-610, and record whether defects were confirmed or only called.

theory.p: Typical objections are that the change affects electrical performance, lacks test coverage, increases cost, delays schedule, or creates thermal or mechanical risk. Answer each with data: solder joint geometry from cross-section or X-ray, thermal profile margin from thermocouple data, mechanical clearance, and test coverage maps. If reliability is questioned, state the relevant qualification status and the residual risk if the change is not made. Use IPC-7711/7721 for rework and repair limits only when discussing repairability, not as a substitute for design change data.

p: The ECN or DCR lists every document that changes and every document that stays the same: gerber revision, BOM revision, stencil file revision, paste lot or type, feeder map, AOI program, reflow profile and work instruction.

Assign a unique change ID, an effective date, and the affected serial or lot range. Mark superseded revisions obsolete in the PLM or document control system, and stop mixed revisions running on the line at the same time.

theory.h: Build an evidence pack a design engineer can audit
p: The pack holds the baseline data, the defect Pareto, representative photos, SPI and AOI results, X-ray or cross-section images, reflow thermocouple traces, rework and scrap records, cost of poor quality, risk matrix, proposed change, verification plan and rollback plan.
Use SI units and state the measurement uncertainty where it affects the decision. For paste and stencil values, cite the paste and equipment datasheet rather than a remembered figure.
Present three options: no change, interim containment, and full design change.

For each, state the expected defect rate, rework time, scrap, schedule impact and residual risk. If the design team resists a land-pattern change, offer a process-only trial first — stencil aperture adjustment, paste type change, or placement pressure change — and record the limits of that trial.
Avoid absolute claims. State conditions, sample sizes and the data behind the projection.

theory.h: Close the change with post-change data
p: After implementation, run a pilot and then a production confirmation.

Compare SPI, AOI, X-ray, functional test, rework, scrap, cycle time and downtime against the baseline. Close the ECN or DCR only when the acceptance criteria are met, the controlled documents are updated and the line runs the new revision.
If the post-change data miss the criteria, reopen the change and identify whether the cause is design, process or execution.

calc.task: A 0402 resistor land pattern on a 1.6 mm board shows tombstoning and insufficient wetting. Baseline over 30 production days: 12000 boards, 2.4 percent boards with rework, average 1.8 defects per reworked board, rework 3.5 min per defect, operator cost 45 EUR/h, scrap 0.3 percent boards, board cost 180 EUR, line downtime 0.5 h/month. Proposed ECN changes land pattern to IPC-7351 nominal and reduces stencil aperture from 0.30 mm x 0.30 mm to 0.25 mm x 0.25 mm; verify against paste datasheet. Pilot predicts boards with rework 0.6 percent, defects per reworked board 1.2, scrap 0.1 percent, downtime 0.2 h/month. Calculate baseline cost of poor quality, projected cost, annual saving, and whether ECN is justified if one-time change cost 8000 EUR.
calc.solution: Step 1: baseline reworked boards = 12000 x 0.024 = 288 boards/month. Step 2: baseline defects = 288 x 1.8 = 518.4 defects/month. Step 3: baseline rework time = 518.4 x 3.5 = 1814.4 min/month = 30.24 h/month. Step 4: baseline rework labor cost = 30.24 x 45 = 1360.8 EUR/month. Step 5: baseline scrap boards = 12000 x 0.003 = 36 boards/month. Step 6: baseline scrap cost = 36 x 180 = 6480 EUR/month. Step 7: baseline downtime cost = 0.5 x 120 = 60 EUR/month, using 120 EUR/h line cost; verify against your line cost model. Step 8: baseline COPQ = 1360.8 + 6480 + 60 = 7900.8 EUR/month. Step 9: projected reworked boards = 12000 x 0.006 = 72 boards/month. Step 10: projected defects = 72 x 1.2 = 86.4 defects/month. Step 11: projected rework time = 86.4 x 3.5 = 302.4 min/month = 5.04 h/month. Step 12: projected rework labor cost = 5.04 x 45 = 226.8 EUR/month. Step 13: projected scrap boards = 12000 x 0.001 = 12 boards/month. Step 14: projected scrap cost = 12 x 180 = 2160 EUR/month. Step 15: projected downtime cost = 0.2 x 120 = 24 EUR/month. Step 16: projected COPQ = 226.8 + 2160 + 24 = 2410.8 EUR/month. Step 17: monthly saving = 7900.8 - 2410.8 = 5490 EUR/month. Step 18: annual saving = 5490 x 12 = 65880 EUR/year. Step 19: payback = 8000 / 5490 = 1.46 months. Step 20: ECN is justified if post-change data confirm the projected defect reduction and no new reliability or test escape risk is introduced.

defect.symptom: After the ECN, AOI reports increased insufficient solder on 0402 resistors during the first 200 boards, while tombstoning decreases.
defect.cause: The new stencil aperture was reduced too far for the paste release window, and the stencil-to-board gap or paste volume was not requalified after the land pattern change.
defect.action: Stop the changeover, retain the old stencil and paste lot for comparison, measure SPI deposit volume and height, requalify the aperture and stencil thickness against the paste datasheet, then run a controlled pilot with thermocouple profiling and X-ray before releasing production.

takeaways: Baseline the problem on a stated sample, because thirty days of data settles objections that opinion cannot.
Close on post-change data, since approval is not the same as effect.
Offer a process-only trial where design resists, because a bounded experiment is easier to approve than a redesign.

mistakes.mistake: Filing a temporary containment as a permanent change
mistakes.instead: Label the duration, because a containment recorded as a fix never gets replaced.

mistakes.mistake: Comparing the pilot against a different product mix
mistakes.instead: Use the same conditions, since mix moves the defect rate.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving two revisions on the line
mistakes.instead: Obsolete the old documents, because mixed revisions make every result ambiguous.

terms.def: A limited production run used to confirm a change before release.
The documented route back to the previous revision if a change fails.
The record of which defects each inspection and test step can detect.
The system that holds current revisions and marks superseded ones obsolete.
